The Texture  SOP  assigns texture UV and W coordinates to the Source geometry for use in texture and bump mapping. It generates multi-layers of texture coordinates.

Fixing Seams & Unrolling  Geometry
NOTE:  the following discussing pertains only to face and hull primitives.
If a texture type requires fixing of seams and the texture is applied to vertices, the wrapped primitives are unrolled before computing the texture coordinates. Unrolling a wrapped primitive turns it into an open primitive whose new vertices use the same points as the vertices they have been uniqued from. Thus, unrolling does not change the point count, nor does it allow cracks to appear further down the road. Explicit unrolling, using the  Primitive SOP , is not required.
The seam fixing is done after computing the texture coordinates. It is required whether textures are applied to vertices or points, and it's done in u, v, or both.
The following texture types require fixing of seams:
Cylindrical  - seams fixed in u.
Polar  - seams fixed in u and v.
Row/col  - seams fixed in u and v.
Spline types :  Uniform ,  Chord Length , and  Average  - seams fixed in u and v.
Note:  When the projection type is  Cylindrical  or  Polar , closed meshes, Bzier & NURBS surfaces will be opened. At least one row/column of vertices will be added (possibly more for NURBS<). This is to prevent poor interpolation of texture coordinates at the seam of the join.

parameters.label: Texture Layer
parameters.name: texlayer
parameters.description: If the geometry has multiple textures layers applied to it, this parameter determines which layer of UV coordinates this Texture  SOP  will effect.

parameters.label: Texture Type
parameters.name: type
parameters.description: ⊞  - The  Face ,  Uniform Spline , and  Arc-Length Spline  texturing methods accept spline curves as well as polygons.

parameters.label: When using one of the spline
parameters.description: based methods, specifying a paste hierarchy in the   Group   field will propagate the computation of texture coordinates to all of its nodes. Projection methods will typically yield smoother texture continuity between pasted surfaces than any of the spline methods. Sometimes it helps ensuring that pasted features are Chord-length parameterized with the  Basis SOP .

parameters.label: Orthographic
parameters.name: texture
parameters.description: Direct projection from  Projection Axis .

parameters.label: XYZ Position
parameters.name: xyzposition
parameters.description: The XYZ position of the vertices will be copied into the UVW values.

parameters.label: Equirectangular Inside (Spherical Polar)
parameters.name: equirectangularin
parameters.description: Applies corrdinates to properly apply an equirectangular texture map to the inside of an object. Useful for skyboxes for example.

parameters.label: Equirectangular Outside (Spherical Polar)
parameters.name: equirectangularout
parameters.description: Applies corrdinates to properly apply an equirectangular texture map to the outside of an object.

parameters.label: Cylindrical
parameters.name: cylin
parameters.description: Wrap cylindrically in  Projection Axis  direction.

parameters.label: Row & Columns
parameters.name: rowcol
parameters.description: For geometry constructed as a mesh (Grid, Sphere, Tube, Skin, and Sweep). The U coordinates are placed along rows, and the V coordinates along columns. This is good for texturing curved meshes such as car fenders where you cannot project from any one axis.

parameters.label: Face
parameters.name: face
parameters.description: Maps a copy of the texture onto every face. You should make points unique using a  Facet SOP , before using this function in the Texture  SOP . The map is graphically projected to each face along its normal, so the texture is oriented properly for each face. However, the map is not scaled to fit each polygon, nor is it distorted by the shape of each polygon. If the geometry changes in size in object space, the texture does not "stick" to the geometry. It is best suited to texturing objects that represent chunks of rock and brick, as the textures will likely not match at the edges between polygons.

parameters.label: Modify Source
parameters.name: modify
parameters.description: If the Source already has texture UV coordinates, they are maintained. You can offset and scale them, however, using  Scale  and  Offset .

parameters.label: Uniform Spline
parameters.name: suniform
parameters.description: This projection type operates only on NURBS and Bzier surfaces. It samples the domain space (i.e. the basis) of each surface uniformly in U and V and assigns those (u,v) values as texture coordinates to the surface points or vertices. To ensure continuity between the texture space of adjacent surfaces insert a  Basis SOP  before the Texture  SOP  and toggle  Concatenate  on to merge the spline bases in U and/or V.

parameters.label: Average Spline
parameters.name: saverage
parameters.description: Stores the average of degree successive knots into the texture attribute. These averages are known as  Greville points . This method and  Uniform Spline  are recommended for pasted surfaces.

parameters.label: Arc Length Spline
parameters.name: sarclen
parameters.description: This method is similar to the  Uniform Spline  method since it relies on the underlying spline basis when computing the texture coordinates. Both methods generate texture coordinates in the same range, bounded by the minimum and maximum knot values. The difference between the two spline methods lies in the spacing between successive texture coordinates. The uniform method samples the parameter space uniformly. The  Arc-Length Spline  method chooses the texture coordinates based on surface arc-lengths.

parameters.label: Since the  Uniform Spline  method relies heavily on the parametric fabric of the surface, the resulting texture will tend to squash and stretch given uneven surface parameterizations. The
parameters.name: Arc
parameters.description: Length Spline  method reduces this effect by relating the texture space directly to the world space of the surface, while ensuring that the size and origin of the generated texture space coincide with those of the underlying domain.

parameters.label: Edge Length
parameters.name: edgelength
parameters.description: Applies to hulls + faces (NURBs/Bezier/ Polygon ).

parameters.label: Perspective From Camera
parameters.name: persp
parameters.description: The texture coordinates are assigned so that the world space of the object can be textured to fit the projection of the camera exactly. If any points are behind the near clipping plane or beyond the far clipping plane, the texture coordinates ( 0, 0, 0 ) are assigned. Note: Unless a Custom Projection matrix is used in the  Camera COMP , the aspect ratio of the projection is assumed to be 1:1. You may need to scale the UVs to match the aspect ratio of your render.

parameters.label: Equidistant Azimuth (Fish Eye 180)
parameters.name: equiazimuth
parameters.description: Applies coordinates for using 180 degree Fish Eye maps.

parameters.label: Equidistant Azimuth (Fish Eye 360)
parameters.name: equiazimuth360
parameters.description: Applies coordinates for using 360 degree Fish Eye maps.

parameters.label: Projection Axis
parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: ⊞  - Axis to project along, or projection method from splines. X, Y, or Z axes.

parameters.label: Camera Name
parameters.name: camera
parameters.description: This is used when the  Perspective From Camera  Texture Type is selected. The menu is used to select which light or camera to project the perspective coordinates from.

parameters.label: Apply to
parameters.name: coord
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select to apply texture coordinates to their Natural Location, Point textures, or  Vertex  textures.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: s
parameters.description: ⊞  - Scales the texture coordinates a specific amount.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: ⊞  - Offsets the texture coordinates a specific amount.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: Rotates the texture coordinates the specified value.

parameters.label: Tip:  Before applying a spline
parameters.description: based texture projection with the Texture  SOP , remap the U and/or V bases of the spline surface (using a  Basis SOP ) between 0 and 1 to ensure a complete mapping of the texture. If a single texture map must be shared by several surfaces, the surface bases should be concatenated prior to being remapped.

parameters.label: Fix Face Seams
parameters.name: fixseams
parameters.description: Attempts to correct texture continuity at face seams.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.name: xord
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the overall transform order for the transformations. The transform order determines the order in which transformations take place. Depending on the order, you can achieve different results using the exact same values. Choose the appropriate order from the menu.

parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.name: rord
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the order of the rotations within the overall transform order.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.name: t
parameters.description: ⊞  - These three fields move the texture coordinates in the three axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.name: r
parameters.description: ⊞  - These three fields rotate the texture coordinates in the three axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: scaletwo
parameters.description: ⊞  - These three fields scale the texture coordinates in the three axes.

parameters.label: Pivot
parameters.name: p
parameters.description: ⊞  - The pivot point for the transformations (not the same as the pivot point in the pivot channels). The pivot point parameters allow you to define the point about which the texture coordinates scale and rotate. Altering the pivot point produces different results depending on the transformation performed.

parameters.label: For example, during a scaling operation, if the pivot point of the texture coordinates is located at:
parameters.description: 1, -1, 0  and you wanted to scale by  0.5  (reduce its size by 50%) the texture would scale toward the pivot point and appear to slide down and to the left.

parameters.label: num_points

parameters.label: num_prims

parameters.label: num_particles

parameters.label: last_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating geometry data on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

Lookup Texture POP * **¿Qué hace?** Este operador es una herramienta para **muestrear datos de una textura (TOP) y aplicarlos como atributos a tus puntos**. Toma dos atributos de tu geometría (generalmente `Lookup Attribute U` y `Lookup Attribute V`) con valores entre 0 y 1, y para cada punto, usa esos valores como coordenadas para buscar píxeles en un TOP (Texture Operator). Los valores RGBA (rojo, verde, azul, alfa) de esos píxeles se convierten en atributos POP. * **Características clave:** *
